name: Glued back
description: A glass or plastic back held on with strong adhesive. The battery and mainboard sit right underneath it.
openingMethod: Warm the edges to soften the glue, lift a corner with a suction cup, then slide thin plastic picks around the edge.
riskNotes: Glass backs can crack while you pry, leaving sharp edges.
Too much heat can damage the battery and other parts.
Picks pushed in too far can tear thin ribbon cables.

name: Clip back
description: A plastic back held on by small clips, sometimes with a few screws. Often found on budget phones.
openingMethod: Remove any visible screws, then run a plastic opening tool around the seam so the clips release one at a time.
riskNotes: Clips snap easily if you force them.
Some screws hide under stickers or the SIM tray.
Metal tools can scratch the case or short parts underneath.

name: Front entry
description: The screen comes off first. The battery and mainboard are reached from the front of the phone.
openingMethod: Remove any screws at the bottom edge, warm the screen edges, then lift the screen slowly without pulling on its cables.
riskNotes: Display cables are short, so the screen cannot be opened far until they are unplugged.
The screen is the most expensive part to break by accident.
Waterproof seals must be replaced when the phone is closed.
